publication.title: Emperor Penguins on Thin Sea Ice
publication.figureLicenseScopeCaveat: Publisher article-wide license and figure credit were observed. An item-specific original NSF permission confirmation was not obtained.

rightsEvidence.basis: Catalog identifies creator and treats work as created in official NSF duties. This is a specific catalog declaration, not a direct newly obtained NSF confirmation.

rightsEvidence.observed: Article copyright statement links CC BY 4.0; Figure 1 expressly credits Deretsky/NSF and links the USAP item. No figure-specific restrictive license or excluded-credit clause was visible.
rightsEvidence.suggestedAttribution: Zina Deretsky / National Science Foundation, Lifecycle of the Emperor Penguin (2006), reproduced as Fig. 1 in Jenouvrier et al. (2023), doi:10.3389/frym.2023.1052262. Article: CC BY 4.0. State any permitted presentation changes.

rightsEvidence.observed: Current NSF visual-media policy distinguishes public-domain assets, contractor work, and third-party assets and says use permission is determined case by case. The fact that an image is on a government website alone is not clearance.

manualVisualInspection.reviewer: research subagent visual inspection of actual downloaded files; not application AI review
manualVisualInspection.fullImageObserved: A dense annual lifecycle illustration on sea ice with blue routes, adult emperor penguin drawings, chicks and English seasonal labels.
manualVisualInspection.relevantRegionCoordinateStatus: Approximate visual location for research only; not approved application annotations.
manualVisualInspection.observedRelevantPixels: Lower-left incubating-adult group includes three adult penguins. Small pale ovals are shown at their foot/belly boundary and emphasized by existing red dashed circles and arrows to an enlarged egg inset. The original graphic labels this incubation stage.
manualVisualInspection.specificStateSupported: A published emperor-penguin incubation schematic explicitly locates the egg at the feet; this is more specific than a generic standing penguin or chick photograph.
limitations: This is an illustration, not photographic documentation.
The small foot-level eggs and feet occupy few pixels within a large multistage graphic; clarity after target-format fitting remains unverified.
The magnified egg next to the group is a callout; it must not be presented as an egg lying free on the ice.
The adjacent hatching region contains a chick and must not be used as evidence of an unhatched egg.
A still schematic supports position/incubation; it does not show the temporal act of laying, transferring or moving an egg.
The original film frame/style was not reconstructed or verified in this research.

pipelineNotes: Keep the original scene text, narration and timing.
Only submit source evidence through the existing full-file acquisition, decode, hashes, rights and actual-image-review gates once calls are authorized/available.
Do not synthesize a contentReview or an accepted source-annotation plan from this research.
Current implementation keeps the full source image fixed and requires 2–4 useful distinct regions with exact scene-substring labels; this very short scene and tiny eggs may legitimately fail.
Use only existing source shapes/callouts if a later reviewer accepts the image; no invented egg, feet, transfer animation, new causal arrows, or reconstructed anatomy.
Preserve the source and copyright marks. Prefer full original resolution over the lower-resolution journal rendering if the recorded rights basis is accepted.
If the rights basis or actual pixel review is rejected, retain the missing scene. Do not force acceptance or replace it with king penguins, chicks, egg specimens, or decorative graphics.
